subject: Re: Commercial alignment request — matching incumbent terms
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@novabyte.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@novabyte.com
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor match request — CloudForge incumbent offer

Hi Mateo,

Quick note from procurement — CloudForge has given us a commercial with a 30% lower per-token list on high-volume inference and a 6-month staged credit equal to ~20% of forecasted spend (see attached CloudForge_quote.pdf). Given our production dependence on low-latency inference and your runtime performance in the POC, we'd like Redwood to make a matching or competitive offer we can take to leadership.

What would Redwood be comfortable offering to match price and migration assistance? We have a conservative procurement timeline: final vendor decision by 6/20.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Platform Engineering, NovaByte
(elena@novabyte.com)
From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena@novabyte.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor match request — CloudForge incumbent offer

Elena —

Thanks for sending the CloudForge quote and the timeline. I'm looping Jordan (sales lead) and Grace (CS/commercial ops) to put together a clean, executable counter that preserves unit economics but gives NovaByte a clear path off the incumbent.

Immediate next steps:
- Jordan: can you draft a counter with a staged credit + pilot discount structure we can sign by 6/18?
- Grace: please flag any legal/finance constraints (credit caps, payback windows) we should bake in.

We can offer migration assistance (1 FTE week of hands-on runbook support + access to our migration playbook) and 30 days of extended telemetry retention for the pilot.

I’ll follow up with a formal PDF.

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena@novabyte.com>, mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood preliminary counter — staged credits + tiered discount (draft)

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the context. Attached is a preliminary commercial (redwood_counter-commercial_v3.pdf) intended to be straightforward and procurement-ready. High-level:
- Price parity approach: match CloudForge per-token rate for first 6 months of committed volume, implemented as a staged credit equal to 18% of 6-month forecast (applied as monthly invoice credits).
- Post-pilot: 10% ongoing discount on committed runrate for the 12-month term.
- Migration assistance: 40 hours of hands-on migration support + runbook and two weeks of priority support during cutover (migration-playbook-stub.docx referenced).
- SLA addendum: 99.9% uptime target with service credits (standard language).

Two asks from procurement will likely come up: an explicit egress credit and an early-termination buyout. We can include a one-time egress credit (up to $15k) tied to documented data movement costs, and an early-termination buyout capped at 20% of remaining committed fees.

Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood preliminary counter — staged credits + tiered discount (draft)

Jordan / Mateo —

A few internal constraints to note before we send anything to procurement:
1) Credit recognition: credits must be amortized against invoices over the 6-month period and cannot be applied retroactively beyond the pilot start date.
2) Credit cap: we should not exceed 20% of 6-month contracted revenue in total credits — the draft at 18% is OK but any upward movement needs exec approval.
3) SLA funding: service credits for SLA breaches are standard, but any unconditional financial indemnity is a non-starter.
4) Egress credit: can do a one-time reimbursement up to $15k with receipts; anything larger needs finance sign-off.

If procurement pushes price parity as a permanent list-level reduction, we should trade that for a minimum 12-month committed volume or an increased pilot prepay (recommended).

Happy to help finalize the wording in the PDF — I’ll annotate the clause set and return.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morales <elena@novabyte.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@novabyte.com
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 07:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood preliminary counter — staged credits + tiered discount (draft)

Team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few procurement notes:
- NovaByte requires price parity for a minimum of 12 months; the staged credit + ongoing discount is acceptable only if the net effective price to NovaByte equals CloudForge for the first 12 months.
- Migration assistance and runbook are important; the procurement team would like a two-week overlap with CloudForge so we don't hit service gaps.
- Egress: our budget for data movement is roughly $22k for the migration window — would Redwood increase the egress credit to cover this?

We can accelerate decisioning if we get a clean term sheet that matches these asks.

Elena
From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena@novabyte.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor match request — final counterproposal and next steps

Elena —

We appreciate the clarity. To keep this executable and protect our economics, here’s Redwood’s final counterproposal:

Offer summary (final):
- Net effective parity: We will deliver net price parity with CloudForge for the first 12 months, implemented as follows:
  * A staged invoice credit equal to 18% of 6-month forecast applied monthly during months 1–6.
  * A supplementary one-time credit at contract signature equal to the delta needed to reach 12-month parity (capped so total credits do not exceed 25% of 12-month committed revenue).
- Ongoing: 10% discount on committed runrate for months 13–24 if NovaByte signs a 24-month commitment.
- Migration & overlap: 60 hours of migration assistance (split across a two-week overlap with CloudForge) and an extended telemetry retention window for 90 days post-cutover.
- Egress: increase one-time egress reimbursement to $20k (receipts required). Anything above triggers finance review.
- ET buyout: early-termination buyout capped at 20% of remaining committed fees.

Conditions:
- Credits amortized over invoice schedule; credits above 20% of 6-month revenue require VP approval (we've capped total credits at 25% of 12-month to allow flexibility).
- Legal standard confidentiality and data handling terms apply.

If this matches your procurement needs, we can prepare a term sheet and a signature-ready SOW by Monday (6/15) for your leadership review.

Next steps:
1) Elena — confirm the $20k egress commitment and that the 2-week CloudForge overlap is acceptable.
2) If confirmed, Jordan and I will circulate the term sheet and SOW.

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
